name: Sinking Ships
label: Revelation
lede: Sinking Ships hid ten copies of their first 7" around Seattle, made one album for Revelation, and called it quits within five years.

eras.title: Ten records, no map
eras.text: Sinking Ships came out of Seattle hardcore in 2004. Danny Hesketh sang, and his brother Jim fronted Champion. The records were objects first: hand-numbered, wrapped in vellum, and in ten cases left somewhere in the city for a stranger to find.

years.p: Hesketh sings, Paul Betinson plays guitar, Colin Horn plays bass. Punknews notes that Hesketh's brother Jim fronted the Seattle band Champion.

years.h: Ten copies go missing on purpose
years.p: The debut 7" on Excursion Records runs to 500 hand-numbered clear copies in vellum covers. Ten speckled copies are hidden around Seattle as a Treasure Hunt Press.

years.h: Meridian gets five songs and a second pressing
years.p: Recorded at the Autopsy Room with Jesse O'Donnell, with 39th and Glisan among the five. Run For Cover repressed it in 2006 as RFC 003.

eras.title: Revelation and a pile of singles
eras.text: Revelation signed them for a debut album that Punknews put among the best, most important hardcore records going. Over the next two years they toured and pressed their own singles in runs of 500.

years.p: Twelve songs in about 29 minutes, recorded by Jesse O'Donnell. Scott Freeman of [[Shook Ones|de5db393-7bcd-4ddc-98c7-1e9a48366f3f]] guests on The Next Time I Go.
years.xp:
Punknews heard latter-era [[Turning Point|19b7cbc9-0898-400a-87d5-bfa47c87487c]] in it and said the guitar tone "requires chiropractic attention." Its closing verdict: "one of the best, most important hardcore bands going."

The review credits the band for skipping posi slogans and straight edge posturing. The songs go to desperation and small-town analysis instead, and the reviewer singles out the closer Wait.

years.p: Four songs on Rev143, including Wallingford Is Still Doomed, named for a Seattle neighborhood.

years.cap: Danny Hesketh in the crowd at a hall show, Seattle area, November 2007
years.h: Spray paint and a European tour
years.p: Safe / Revenge, cut at Sound West in Tacoma, is the first release on Sinking Ships Records: 500 copies, a handful in badly spray-painted covers sold on tour in Europe.

years.h: Blue at Sound and Fury, gold by mail
years.p: Out of Touch / Bee Honda, the second Sinking Ships Records single, comes in 250 blue copies sold at the festival and 250 gold ones by mail order only.

years.h: Rainfest, Comeback Kid, and a Japan-only split
years.p: They play Rainfest and share bills with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]], [[Down to Nothing|fac027c9-e8db-4546-9515-9d48d1a7185c]], [[Shook Ones|de5db393-7bcd-4ddc-98c7-1e9a48366f3f]] and [[Blacklisted|00330ad2-6d94-4957-b3b0-7ca1ea6f6fd6]]. A split with As We Let Go and My Love comes out only in Japan, on Alliance Trax.

years.h: One album, a stack of 7"s, and that's it
years.p: Sinking Ships break up at the end of 2008, four years after they started.

eras.title: Back for a night
eras.text: In 2013 the core of the band came back, and Disconnecting was remastered and reissued.

years.cap: Danny Hesketh in the crowd at the reunion show, Seattle, May 23, 2013
yt: Reunion show, Rain Fest pre-show, May 23, 2013
years.h: The reunion: five years after the split
years.p: Hesketh, Betinson and Horn bring the band back in 2013, and Disconnecting gets a remastered reissue.
